identity.name: Copenhagen Business School Danish Government Scholarship
identity.issuing_authority: Copenhagen Business School, from a limited number of Danish government scholarships allocated to CBS each year

verifiable_urls.kind: master application and admission page (Scholarship panel)

records.description: CBS receives a limited number of Danish government scholarships each year to fund highly qualified full-degree students from outside the EU/EEA. Each scholarship combines a full tuition fee waiver with a monthly stipend of DKK 8,000 towards living costs, granted for a maximum of 22 months. Around 25 scholarships are awarded per year, and the award is based on motivation and academic background rather than financial need.

official.program_type: Government-financed tuition waiver plus monthly living stipend, awarded by CBS
eligibility: Need a student residence permit to study at CBS
Pay the application fee by the application deadline, unless you hold a bachelor degree from a Danish educational institution
Upload a personal statement and apply online in the Application Portal
May not receive a scholarship if you are eligible for SU (Danish State Educational Grant) or any other type of public support in Denmark
benefits: Monthly stipend of DKK 8,000 to assist with living costs in Denmark
Maximum duration of 22 months, starting 1 September the year you are accepted (1 February if accepted in the Winter application round)
The grant is taxable in Denmark according to the rules governing income from grants and tax exemption for developing countries
selection_criteria: The scholarship is aimed at highly qualified students and is not given based on financial needs
Your academic record and your English proficiency will be assessed together with your personal statement
Your life and work experience will also be considered in the selection process
A selection committee will assess the scholarship applications and in some cases decide to interview an applicant
The committee makes the final decision as to who is offered a scholarship
application_process: Apply for admission to a CBS master programme no later than the deadline via the Application Portal
Indicate that you wish to be considered for the CBS scholarship in the Application Portal
Upload a personal statement of a maximum of 2 pages explaining your purpose and reasons for choosing CBS and a particular programme
If you apply for a programme where the selection process includes a personal statement, the scholarship personal statement counts for both purposes
Pay the application fee by the deadline (or upload documentation if you are exempt)
official.duration: Maximum 22 months, starting 1 September of the acceptance year (1 February for the Winter round)
key_dates: Scholarship application deadline: 15 October at 23:59 CET (Winter application round)
Admission application deadline for scholarship consideration: 15 January 23:59 CET (15 October for the Winter round)
Scholarship applicants notified by 15 March at the latest via the Application Portal (10 December for the Winter round)

deadlines.label: Scholarship application deadline (Winter round)
deadlines.note: CBS sets 15 October at 23:59 CET as the scholarship application deadline for the Winter application round; the summer-round equivalent is 15 January 23:59 CET.

deadlines.label: Scholarship decision notification
deadlines.note: Winter-round scholarship applicants are notified by 10 December at the latest via the Application Portal; summer-round notifications are by 15 March.

deadlines.label: Tuition fee payment deadline (first semester)
deadlines.note: Deadline for paying the first-semester tuition fee or documenting exemption, if the scholarship is not awarded.

verification.deadline_note: There are two rounds. For scholarship consideration you must apply for admission no later than 15 January 23:59 CET for the summer round or 15 October 23:59 CET for the Winter round, and the scholarship application itself closes at the same time as the application fee deadline (15 October at 23:59 CET for the Winter round).
verification.application_cycle: Two annual admission rounds: Summer (apply by 15 January, notified by 15 March) and Winter (apply by 15 October, notified by 10 December)
verification.tuition_coverage_note: Each scholarship includes a tuition fee waiver.
verification.english_requirement: Your academic record and your English proficiency are assessed together with your personal statement; the scholarship page does not publish a minimum score. Programme-level language requirements must be fulfilled by the application deadline.
verification.status_note: CBS describes a standing annual allocation of approximately 25 government scholarships per year for non-EU/EEA full-degree students. Deadlines for both rounds are published as absolute dates rather than as a dated call that opens and closes.
not_confirmed: exact DKK net amount after tax (CBS states the grant is taxable and that the DKK 8,000 is gross)
any travel, installation or insurance allowance
a minimum English test score for the scholarship itself
the number of scholarships reserved per programme or the interview pass rate
documents: Personal statement, maximum 2 pages, uploaded in the Application Portal - this is mandatory for scholarship applicants
Application fee payment receipt or documentation of exemption
All admission documentation required by the programme, including documentation of English proficiency

applicant_utility.description: This is one of the few Danish packages that pairs a full tuition waiver with a real monthly stipend, and CBS takes roughly 25 people a year across all graduate programmes - so treat it as a lottery you enter inside your admission application, not a separate funding decision. The critical mechanic is that you must tick the scholarship box in the Application Portal and upload a two-page personal statement; if you apply for a programme that also uses a personal statement in selection, the same document serves both purposes. Because the stipend is taxable and the grant runs a maximum of 22 months, plan for the gap beyond that period and for a tax bill.
eligibility_tips: The citizenship bar is absolute: non-EU, non-EEA and non-Swiss only, and you must need a student residence permit. EU/EEA applicants are excluded outright.
If you qualify for SU (Danish State Educational Grant) or any other Danish public support, you may not receive this scholarship - check your SU status before counting on it.
Paying the application fee by the deadline is itself an eligibility condition, unless you hold a Danish bachelor degree.
application_tips: Indicate the scholarship wish in the Application Portal itself. Applying alone does not enter you into the scholarship pool.
Write one strong personal statement that works for both admission and scholarship - CBS explicitly lets a single statement serve both, and it must be personal and specific rather than generic.
Use the full two pages. CBS describes academic performance as very important but also weighs life and work experience, internships and extracurricular activity, so give those room.
If you are offered a place but not the scholarship, you will receive an invoice for the first tuition payment - budget for that possibility before you commit.
documents: Personal statement (max 2 pages) - the single document that decides both admission and scholarship outcomes.
Application fee receipt or exemption documentation, due by the same 15 October deadline as the scholarship application in the Winter round.
Documentation of English proficiency, which must be valid by the application deadline for the programme itself.
mistakes_to_avoid: Keeping the scholarship quietly in mind and applying normally - the portal flag is the entry ticket.
Submitting a generic statement. CBS says the statement must prove you are well-informed and have put a lot of thought into your choice of CBS and that specific programme.
Changing programme after being awarded. Scholarships are awarded for a specific master programme and you must stay enrolled in it.
Falling more than 30 ECTS behind your study plan. CBS checks study activity each semester and will withdraw the grant and re-bill tuition if you are not active.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: Apply by 15 January for the summer round or 15 October for the Winter round, and note the scholarship decision lands months later - 15 March or 10 December - while the first tuition instalment is due 17 December. That gap is a genuine cash-flow trap: if you are offered a place but not the scholarship you must find the tuition money immediately, and CBS notes the residence permit process cannot start until tuition is received. Also note the grant is capped at 22 months and is not extended beyond the standard study period except in extraordinary circumstances such as severe illness.

identity.name: Aalborg University International Student Scholarship (tuition fee waiver and monthly stipend)
identity.issuing_authority: Aalborg University, financed by the Danish Government

verifiable_urls.kind: master finance, fees and scholarships page

records.description: Each September intake, Aalborg University grants a limited number of scholarships - approximately 15 per year - to individually selected applicants from outside the EU/EEA. A scholarship consists of a tuition fee waiver plus a monthly stipend intended to cover living expenses for the four semesters of a master's programme. All non-EU applicants are considered automatically when applying to a master's programme, so there is no separate scholarship application.

official.program_type: Government-financed tuition fee waiver plus monthly living stipend, awarded by Aalborg University
eligibility: Applicant is a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA
Is required to pay tuition fees, i.e. does not hold one of the residence permits that exempt non-EU/EEA students from application and tuition fees
Applying to a master's programme at Aalborg University
EU/EEA students cannot apply for scholarships at AAU
Aalborg University does not offer tuition waivers or scholarships for bachelor's programmes
Scholarships are granted per September intake only
benefits: Monthly stipend aimed at covering living expenses for the four semesters of the master's programme
Stipend rate for new students in 2026: 11,225 DKK / 1,503 EUR per month
Possible tuition fee refund if the fee was paid before the scholarship decision
Stipend may be paid retroactively from 1 September where a Danish CPR number, NemKonto and tax registration are not yet in place
selection_criteria: Scholarships are granted to individually selected applicants from non-EU/EEA countries based on strategic considerations and academic qualifications
Academic qualifications transcend national borders and are essentially global
All non-EU applicants are automatically considered when applying to a master's programme
application_process: Apply to a master's programme through the AAU Application Portal (dans.stads.dk); no separate scholarship application exists or is accepted
Pay the non-refundable application fee of 150 EUR (1,150 DKK) unless exempt, and upload the receipt to all applications in the Application Portal
Await the scholarship decision, communicated no later than the beginning of July
If tuition was paid before the scholarship decision and the scholarship is then granted, the tuition fee is refunded
official.duration: Four semesters, the standard duration of a master's degree at AAU; no further stipend beyond the first two years of study
key_dates: Scholarship decisions communicated to all applicants by the beginning of July at the latest
Tuition payment deadline for newly admitted students: approximately 14 days after admission information
Semester tuition deadlines: 1 January for the spring semester and 1 August for the autumn semester

deadlines.label: Scholarship decision notification
deadlines.note: AAU states it will inform all applicants about the scholarship decision by the beginning of July at the latest, though it may be earlier. No exact calendar date is published.

deadlines.label: Tuition payment deadline (newly admitted)
deadlines.note: Newly admitted students receive payment instructions in a separate letter and must pay within approximately 14 days; this deadline cannot be extended.

verification.deadline_note: There is no scholarship application and therefore no scholarship deadline. AAU publishes only the decision date (by the beginning of July) and the tuition payment deadline (approximately 14 days after admission information, which cannot be extended).
verification.application_cycle: September intake only; approximately 15 scholarships granted each year
verification.tuition_coverage_note: A scholarship consists of a tuition fee waiver and a monthly stipend aimed at covering living expenses.
verification.english_requirement: Programme-level language requirements apply for English-taught master's programmes; no scholarship-specific English score is published.
verification.status_note: AAU describes the award as a standing September-intake allocation of approximately 15 scholarships per year, awarded by the university on behalf of the Danish Government, with automatic consideration for all non-EU master's applicants.
not_confirmed: any travel, installation or insurance allowance
the application deadline that governs scholarship consideration (it follows the master's admission deadline, which is not published on this page)
the tax treatment of the stipend (AAU notes tax may apply but links out)
which programmes are strategic priorities for the current cycle
documents: Application fee receipt of 150 EUR (1,150 DKK) uploaded to all applications in the Application Portal, unless exempt
Standard master's admission documentation for the chosen programme

applicant_utility.description: The single most useful fact here is that you cannot apply for this scholarship separately - every non-EU applicant to a master's programme is considered automatically, so your admission application is your scholarship application. That also means you cannot influence the outcome beyond your application materials, and AAU explicitly warns not to rely on receiving one: roughly 15 awards against a full non-EU intake is a low hit rate. Because AAU cannot guarantee the decision arrives before the tuition deadline, and tuition is refundable if the scholarship is later granted, the realistic strategy is to pay and hope rather than to wait.
eligibility_tips: You must be liable for tuition fees. If you hold a permanent residence permit, a humanitarian protection permit, a Ukraine-displacement permit or one of the other listed permits, you are fee-exempt and therefore outside the scholarship scheme.
EU/EEA citizens cannot apply, and there are no bachelor's scholarships at all - this is a master's-only, September-intake-only award.
Scholarships are granted per September intake, so a February start does not enter you into the pool.
application_tips: Put your effort into the master's application itself, since that is the only material the scholarship committee sees. There is no extra form to optimise.

Pay the 150 EUR (1,150 DKK) application fee promptly and upload the receipt to every application in the portal - it is non-refundable even if you later withdraw, and it doubles as a de facto application deadline.

Arrange the Danish logistics early: AAU notes you need a CPR number, NemKonto and tax registration before the stipend can be paid, and until then it is paid retroactively from 1 September. Do not plan your first month's budget around receiving money on time.
documents: Application fee receipt uploaded to all applications - AAU is explicit that one fee covers a maximum of three applications for a specific intake.
Programme admission documents as required by the chosen master's programme.
Nothing extra for the scholarship itself.
mistakes_to_avoid: Waiting for the scholarship decision before paying tuition. AAU cannot guarantee the decision precedes the tuition deadline, and the deadline cannot be extended.
Relying on the scholarship as your funding plan. AAU states plainly that it does not advise relying solely on receiving a scholarship.
Assuming the stipend covers Danish living costs. AAU warns the scholarship may not cover all living expenses and expects you to supplement with savings, a home-country loan or a student job.
Applying as an EU/EEA citizen or to a bachelor's programme - both are excluded.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: There is no scholarship deadline to miss, which is either reassuring or a trap depending on how you plan: the binding date is the tuition payment deadline roughly 14 days after your admission information, and AAU says it cannot be extended. Scholarship decisions land by the beginning of July at the latest, so expect a long period of uncertainty. If your studies are prolonged beyond four semesters you will not receive further stipend, so the award is a two-year funding floor rather than a guarantee for your whole degree.
